cards.what: Buy Now on a piece already in the bag sends it to checkout once, not twice, and still works if Shopify has lost it.
cards.shoppers: With only that piece in the bag, Add to cart then Buy Now checks out 1 at full price, not 2 at 15% off. If Shopify lost it, Buy Now puts it back and opens checkout, instead of failing.
cards.meta: One add to cart fewer, and the checkout start counts one piece fewer (bracelet alone: ₹2,399, not ₹4,798). Where checkout used to fail, Meta now gets an add to cart and a checkout start.
cards.ask: Should Add to cart then Buy Now on the same piece check out 1 at full price, rather than 2 at 15% off as today?
cards.why: Changes discount, Meta counts; approve with 'Buy Now with a picked quantity raises a bag line to it before checkout'.

cards.what: On the outfit page, Buy Now sends the picked quantity to checkout, rather than adding it on top of the outfit already in the bag.
cards.shoppers: A shopper with the outfit in the bag who picks 3 now gets 3 at checkout, not 4. Jewellery pages are unchanged, and outfits are sold out today.
cards.meta: Meta's add to cart counts the 2 extra pieces asked for, not 3, and the checkout start counts the 3 in the bag. If stock is short, add to cart still over-reports, as before.
cards.why: A clear fix for the wrong quantity at checkout, and outfits are sold out on the live shop today.

cards.what: Undo straight after Remove now brings the piece back safely, and a piece Shopify already dropped no longer empties the whole bag.
cards.shoppers: Undo straight after Remove brings the piece back and keeps the rest of the bag; before, a piece or the whole bag could be lost. A piece Shopify already dropped no longer empties the bag.
cards.meta: Undo now always sends one add to cart, for a piece that stays. Where a dropped piece used to empty the bag, Meta may now see extra add to cart, checkout start and payment step events.
cards.why: Clear bug fix; approve with 'Removing a bag line Shopify no longer has drops it without an error', or neither.

cards.what: Removing a piece from the bag that Shopify has already dropped now just takes it out, instead of an error or emptying the bag.
cards.shoppers: Remove on a piece Shopify has already dropped now takes it out quietly and keeps the rest of the bag. Before, the whole bag was emptied.
cards.meta: The next checkout start and payment step count only the pieces really left, for example the bracelet at ₹2,399. Before, the bag was empty, so neither was sent.
cards.why: Low-risk bug fix that only runs when Shopify says the piece is gone; pairs with the Undo card.

cards.what: For rings Shopify does not list in sizes, the size a shopper picks now reaches Fastrr orders; before, no size was passed on.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.why: Fixes missing ring sizes on Fastrr orders; worth checking the next real ring order shows the size.

cards.what: Checkout now records which ad campaign brought the shopper, for both Fastrr and Shopify's own checkout.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.ask: If a shopper arrives from one ad then opens another in the same tab, should checkout credit the first campaign (as built) rather than the latest?
cards.why: Low risk, but crediting the first or latest campaign is an open choice for you.

cards.what: When Fastrr cannot start, Shopify's own checkout now opens directly instead of bouncing through extra pages and reloading the site.
cards.shoppers: When Fastrr cannot start, Shopify's checkout opens about 3 seconds sooner, without the site flashing up in between. The order summary and discount are the same.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.why: Low-risk speed fix; the old forwarding page stays as a safety net for old links.

cards.what: When checking out a single piece, an old Buy 2 or Buy 3 code is taken off the Shopify cart used as the fallback.
cards.shoppers: Shopify's fallback checkout no longer carries an old Buy 2 code that does not apply. The price is the same.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.why: Very low risk: it never slows checkout and cannot change the price.

cards.what: When the bag holds other pieces, Buy Now sends only the piece being viewed to checkout, at its own price.
cards.shoppers: With the hoops in the bag, Buy Now on the bracelet shows the bracelet alone at ₹2,399, not both at 15% off. Both pieces stay in the bag.
cards.meta: In that example, the checkout start Meta gets is ₹2,399 with 1 item, not ₹3,698 with 2. Add to cart events are unchanged.
cards.ask: Optional: should Buy Now send only the viewed piece at its own price, or the whole bag with its Buy 2 / Buy 3 discount, as today?
cards.why: A real business choice: less discount and a smaller checkout on Buy Now; this card is optional.

corrections.problem: 'Sends exactly that number' overstated it. The full text says checkout gets fewer when stock is short (2 left gives 2), and gets the bag's own amount when the bag already holds more than was picked (3 in the bag, 2 picked gives 3). Reworded to say Buy Now sends the picked quantity instead of adding it on top of what is in the bag.

'Without losing or wiping other pieces' got the old bug wrong. Before, the piece being undone was the one that got lost (the hoops), or the whole bag was wiped. Other pieces were never lost on their own. 'Reliably' was also dropped. Now says Undo brings the piece back and keeps the rest of the bag.

Covered too much. The full text says the change only applies to rings Shopify does not list in sizes (the adjustable rings, Droplet Open Ring and rings sold only in US 6). It does not apply to every ring size. Now limited to those rings.

Said Add to cart then Buy Now gives 1 at full price, not 2 at 15% off, without saying this is when only that piece is in the bag. With other pieces in the bag the full text says it becomes 2 at 15% off instead of 3 at 25% off. It also said 'instead of the bag emptying', which goes too far: when Shopify has lost the whole bag, the other pieces still leave it. The fixed text limits the first sentence to a bag holding only that piece and says 'instead of failing'.

'The checkout start counts 1 piece, not 2' was stated for every case, but it is only true when the piece is alone in the bag. With the hoops in the bag it goes from 3 to 2. Reworded to 'one piece fewer', with the bracelet-alone amounts kept as the example.

It was 21 words, over the 20-word limit. Shortened, keeping the reason (discount and Meta counts change) and the plain title of the change it must be approved with (checked against the shop's change list).

cards.what: When the site is built for publishing, the hidden browser that pre-draws its pages stops sending fake product views to Meta.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Each publish stops adding fake product views from the build. The audit counted 154 per publish, so Ads Manager may show fewer product views, while real shopper views are unaffected.
cards.why: Removes fake product views, rated low risk; tested on sample pages, though a full publish build was not run.

cards.what: The server's copy of each event now goes to Meta only from the real shop, matching the browser's copy.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Previews, test runs and site builds no longer send events to Meta through the server. Shop pages send them as before, but a page missing a small built-in setting would send none.
cards.why: Stops test events reaching Meta, rated low risk; the live product page was checked and has the needed setting.

cards.what: Once deployed, the relay that passes events to Meta will only pass on events from nairaflore.com pages.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Events from previews, test copies, look-alike sites or with no page address will be dropped. In testing, events from shop pages passed through unchanged.
cards.why: Blocks non-shop events, rated low risk; any new shop web address would need adding to the list.

cards.what: Once deployed, the relay to Meta accepts only events from the shop's own website, and only the nine event types the shop sends.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Events from other websites, or of a type the shop's pages do not send (such as purchase), will be refused; any new type added later must join the list. In testing, genuine shop events passed through unchanged.
cards.why: Refuses outside and made-up events, rated low risk, though a script can still pretend to come from the shop.

cards.what: Tells Meta the exact colour and size a product page opens on, such as the Silver from a Silver ad, instead of the default one.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Product views name the item on screen, such as Star Point Band Silver US 6, not Gold US 5, once per piece, usually at the same price. Newly added colours and a few other links report about a second later.
cards.why: A low-risk fix so Meta hears the right item; checkout and the number of product views are unchanged.

cards.what: When a shopper taps a wishlist heart, Meta is now told the exact catalogue item and its price.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Wishlist adds now name the exact catalogue item and carry its price, such as ₹1,300 for Molten Bloom Hoops. Still one event per add, and none on removal.
cards.why: Gives Meta the exact item and price for wishlist adds; counts unchanged, rated low risk.

cards.what: Every search a shopper settles on is now reported to Meta once, including searches with no results or closed straight away.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Ads Manager may show more searches, as searches with no results or closed straight away now count, each once. A shopper pausing a second mid-word may send that partial word.
cards.why: Fixes searches that were missed; rated low risk, though a mid-word pause can count as a search.

cards.what: Sets Meta's browser id on the shopper's device as soon as a shop page opens, rather than waiting for Meta's own script to load.
cards.shoppers: Nothing visible changes. A Meta browser-id cookie, kept for 90 days, is now saved as the page opens, including for shoppers who leave quickly or block Meta's script.
cards.meta: The first product view sent before Meta's script loads now carries the browser id. Shoppers who block Meta's script now send a shop-made id with every server copy and at checkout; before, they sent none.
cards.why: Low risk with checkout unchanged; Meta says its script keeps this id, but that could not be tested.

cards.what: The shop's visitor id and Meta ad-click id are now readable on the shop's Shopify checkout pages, not just the main site.
cards.shoppers: Nothing visible changes. Returning visitors keep the same ids, and the visitor id's expiry now renews on each visit.
cards.meta: Events from the shop's pages are unchanged. Shopify's checkout can now read the visitor id and the ad-click id.
cards.why: Rated low to medium risk because it changes cookie handling for every shopper.

cards.what: The privacy page and the two consent boxes now say a member's phone number, not just email, is scrambled and shared with Meta.
cards.shoppers: Shoppers see new wording on the privacy page and the sign-up and account details consent boxes. It says email, and phone if added, are scrambled and shared with Meta only to match them.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.ask: Is the new wording what you want members to read, or should the shop stop sending phone numbers and keep the policy email-only?
cards.why: You must confirm the privacy wording; the email-only option would need a separate change.

cards.what: Stops the bag's Checkout button from also telling Meta the shopper reached the payment step; it now reports only the checkout start.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Each Checkout tap now sends only a checkout start, so Ads Manager may show fewer payment step events. Those then come only from the other sender, likely Shiprocket, so orders via Shopify's checkout (about 1 in 50) may have none.
cards.ask: Should Meta hear our checkout start, switching off the other sender's (likely Shiprocket) if possible, as recommended, or that sender's own, which needs a small code change?
cards.why: Check first that Shiprocket's Meta setting for the payment step is on, since it becomes the only source.

cards.what: The value Meta is told at checkout start becomes the bag's actual Total after discounts, instead of the price before discount.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: In Ads Manager, checkout-start values drop for discounted bags; a two-piece BUY2 bag goes from ₹3,398 to ₹2,888. Any custom conversion based on that value would shift.
cards.ask: This change is optional: do you want Meta's checkout-start value to show the discounted bag Total rather than the pre-discount price?
cards.why: Optional, and it lowers reported checkout-start values for discounted bags in Ads Manager.

cards.what: Puts each piece's Shopify product code back into the hidden product details on its page, and corrects two bracelets whose codes were swapped.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Product views may carry these codes to Meta through Meta's automatic setting, which the site leaves on; whether it is on in Meta's own settings was not checked. Google sees the same codes.
cards.ask: Are you happy for supplier product codes, such as B00681C or YF5214-G-5, to sit in every product page's code where Google and Meta can read them?
cards.why: Supplier codes become readable in every product page's code; only you can decide if that is acceptable.

cards.what: When a product view is still waiting for Shopify and the shopper moves on, Meta is told the piece's own page, not the next one.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Only the page address in Meta's server copy changes, for the few product views still waiting for Shopify, at most 3 seconds, when the shopper changes page or picks a colour. Item, value and timing stay the same.
cards.ask: Optional: do you want this, knowing it can only be taken if 'Meta's server copy only reports from the real shop' is approved too?
cards.why: Optional and recommended, but it needs 'Meta's server copy only reports from the real shop' approved as well.

corrections.problem: Called it a 'test browser'. The full text says it is the capture browser that pre-draws pages while the site is built, not a test tool.
Left out the testing gap the risk text names: only the blocking rule was replayed on 3 product pages, and the full publish build was not run.
Left out the named risk that a page served without the inline setting would send no server copies to Meta. 'Exactly as before' was also stronger than what was measured.
Rewrote it around the actual safeguard: the live product page was checked and has the setting that server copies now depend on.
Left out the named risk that if the shop ever serves pages on another web address, that address must be added to the list or its events are dropped.
Left out that any new event type added to the site later must also be added to the relay's list, or it will be refused.
Left out the named risk that a script can fake the website check. Without it, 'only from the shop's own website' overstates the protection.
Left out a change in what Meta is told on every plain visit: the plain pages of sized rings now report the US 6 item they open on, not US 5.

Left out the named risk that a piece with several variants gives its lead variant's code whatever colour is on screen. Also took the second example code out of the meta line and made clear that Google reads the codes from the page rather than receiving product views.

'at the same price' was overstated. With its fix included, a page opened without its pre-drawn copy changes the value sent (Star Point Band ₹999 to ₹799; a colour the piece is not sold in ₹2,949 to ₹1,300). Changed to 'usually at the same price'. The delayed sending also covers more than newly added colours (pages without a pre-drawn copy, colours the piece is not sold in), so the line now says 'newly added colours and a few other links'.
Left out the risk the card names: Meta says its script keeps an id that is already set, but this could not be tested. The line now says so, while keeping low risk and checkout unchanged.

Left out the named risk that on the Shopify checkout (about 1 in 50 orders) the site no longer sends any payment step event, and it is not checked whether Shopify sends its own. Added. Also made the drop in payment step events in Ads Manager the first point.
Said the other sender's event would be 'switched off', but the card says that is only possible if Shiprocket offers the switch. Added 'if possible'.

'for the few product views that waited up to 3 seconds' suggested every delayed view changes address. Only views where the shopper changed page or picked a colour during the wait (at most 3 seconds) are affected. Reworded.

cards.what: The bag now shows Shopify's current price for each piece, so bag prices and the Total always match what checkout charges.
cards.shoppers: Bag prices, the Total and the Buy 2 / Buy 3 saving now match what checkout charges. A saved Mesh Band Ring that showed ₹699 now shows ₹799, Shopify's price.
cards.meta: Checkout start and payment step values now follow Shopify's price, for example ₹699 becoming ₹799 or ₹2,449 becoming ₹1,899. Add to cart keeps the page's price, except Undo in the bag, which sends Shopify's.
cards.ask: Do you accept that checkout start, payment step and bag Undo add to cart values sent to Meta follow Shopify's current price, not the price shown when added?
cards.why: Fixes bag totals that disagreed with checkout, but changes checkout values Meta sees, which you must accept.

cards.what: Before the live catalogue loads, the site now shows Shopify's prices, stock, photos and suggestions from 30 Oct, not a much older copy.
cards.shoppers: For a moment before the catalogue loads, cards show Shopify's 30 Oct prices, for example Woven Gold Hoops ₹1,299, not ₹2,349. Sold-out pieces read SOLD OUT, move to the grid's end, and their pages offer only Reserve now.
cards.meta: In that moment, product view, add to cart, checkout start and payment step values use the 30 Oct prices, such as ₹2,349 becoming ₹1,299. Sold-out pieces no longer send add to cart or checkout start.
cards.ask: Do you accept using Shopify's 30 Oct prices and stock, for shoppers and Meta, before the catalogue loads, and asking for a price refresh after each reprice or restock?
cards.why: Fixes out-of-date early prices, but changes values Meta sees and needs a refresh after every reprice or restock.

cards.what: Meta is told about an add to cart only when Shopify actually adds a piece, and only for the quantity added.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Taps that added nothing no longer count as add to cart, so you may see fewer in Ads Manager. With one piece left, three taps sent 3 before, now 1.
cards.ask: Is it OK to stop telling Meta about add to cart taps that added nothing, and to count only the pieces actually added?
cards.why: Low risk fix for add to carts that never happened, but Meta may see fewer add to carts.

cards.what: Tapping '+' in the bag to add another of a piece will now be reported to Meta as an add to cart.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: Each accepted '+' now sends one add to cart at the bag line's price, so you may see more add to carts. A '+' blocked by stock, or any '−', sends nothing.
cards.ask: Is it OK for '+' in the bag to count as an add to cart for Meta, one per piece added?
cards.why: A choice about what counts as an add to cart; it can raise the add to cart numbers Meta sees.

cards.what: When Shopify marks an adjustable ring sold out, its page and reel row swap Add to cart and Buy Now for Reserve now on WhatsApp.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes today: all 14 adjustable rings were in stock at the last check. If one sells out, shoppers see only Reserve now instead of Add to cart and a Buy Now that cannot complete.
cards.meta: Nothing changes today. Once a ring sells out, Meta gets no add to cart or empty checkout start for it; the early prices and sold-out card alone does the same.
cards.ask: If an adjustable ring sells out, keep Add to cart and Buy Now (decline), or switch it to Reserve now on WhatsApp (approve)?
cards.why: A business choice that changes nothing today; it matters only when an adjustable ring sells out.

corrections.problem: The only example was a price drop (Heartline), which suggests every first-paint price goes down. Some go up, for example Mesh Band Ring ₹699 to ₹799, so that example is now added.

It left out that payment step values change too. It also used the Woven Gold Hoops ₹2,349 to ₹1,299 figure for checkout values, but that figure was only measured for product view and add to cart. 'From that moment' could also be read as 'permanently from now on'. The text is now limited to 'in that moment', the example is tied to product view and add to cart, and payment step and checkout are named.

It left out that the values sent to Meta change, which the card's own question names. It also turned the price refresh reminder into a separate thing to agree to. Meta values are now in the question, and the refresh is worded as a condition.
It said a refresh is needed only after repricing. The card says to re-run it after restocking too.

Approve was too strong. The change lowers the add to cart count in Ads Manager, and that is a shift in ad numbers the owner should weigh. The card also asks the owner a direct question. Changed to Your call.
Rewritten to match the Your call advice. It now says plainly that Meta may see fewer add to carts.
It left out that approving the card on prices before the catalogue loads already stops this add to cart and empty checkout start. So this card only changes what Meta is told if that card is declined.
It left out the effect the card names on Google: a sold-out adjustable ring is reported to Google as out of stock instead of in stock.

The question named only the checkout values. The card's risk text says the owner must accept three Meta changes: the checkout start value, the payment step value, and the add to cart sent when Undo puts a piece back in the bag. The ask now names all three.
It said Undo was an exception to 'Add to cart keeps the page's price' but did not say what Undo sends instead. It now says Undo sends Shopify's price (measured 699 to 799).

'Today's prices' overstated how current the copy is. It is Shopify as of 30 Oct and has already gone out of date once (Roman Numeral Trio Ring). 'Not Buy Now' also left out that Add to cart goes too, since the pages offer only Reserve now. Added the Woven Gold Hoops ₹2,349 to ₹1,299 example from the card.
'Today's prices' became the 30 Oct prices, for the same reason. The vague 'checkout and payment values' now uses the required terms 'checkout start' and 'payment step'.
The card's question also asks the owner to accept that the values sent to Meta in that moment use these prices. The draft ask left Meta out.
It said only Buy Now is replaced. The page loses both Add to cart and Buy Now, and the reel row loses its 'Add' button (measured '₹1,199 Add' to 'Pre-order Reserve').
It left out that Add to cart is also removed from the page, not only Buy Now.

'Its Buy Now no longer sends' was wrong, because approving removes Buy Now altogether. It also left out the card's point that approving the early prices and sold-out card alone already stops these add to cart and empty checkout start events.

cards.what: Old Shopify web addresses that showed 'Coming soon' now open a real page on the shop, keeping the ad's tracking.
cards.shoppers: 23 kinds of old Shopify link that showed 'Coming soon' now open a real page, such as the product or FAQs. Two old collections open the outfits page, not the jewellery; account links and unknown addresses still show Coming soon.
cards.meta: Most redirected visits now send two page views instead of one, the old address then the real page, with the ad's click id kept. A product opened from an old collection link also sends a new product view.
cards.why: Fixes dead old links, but is rated low to medium risk and adds page views in Meta.

cards.what: When a product page fails to load, the 'Browse the collection' link and the phone's Back button now actually leave the error panel.
cards.shoppers: Tapping 'Browse the collection' on the 'This page didn't load' panel now opens the collection instead of leaving the panel stuck on screen. Ordinary visits look and behave the same.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.why: A clear fix for shoppers stuck on the error panel, marked low risk.

cards.what: Makes sure the page a shopper reaches from the error panel is counted as a page view in Meta.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes for shoppers.
cards.meta: After a shopper leaves the error panel, the page they reach now sends one page view, where before nothing was sent. Ordinary visits send exactly what they do today.
cards.why: Low-risk fix that counts a missed page view; ordinary visits send exactly the same.

cards.what: When a catalogue ad names a metal, stone or birthstone month, the product page opens on that choice instead of the default.
cards.shoppers: A Birthstone Heart Necklace ad for May now opens on May with its emerald photo, not January. Rings open on US 6 as today; a sold-out month would show as sold out.
cards.meta: Only for the birthstone month ads: add to cart and checkout start now name May instead of January, at the same ₹699. Product views and all ring links are reported exactly as today.
cards.why: Fixes month ads opening on the wrong month; with its fixes, rings and everything else behave as today.

cards.what: A longer form of the homepage address now opens the homepage instead of 'Coming soon', keeping the ad's tracking.
cards.shoppers: Shoppers arriving on that address keep seeing the homepage, instead of 'Coming soon' appearing over it after about 8.5 seconds.
cards.meta: Visits to that address now count two page views instead of one: that address, then the homepage, with the ad's click id kept. No other events change.
cards.why: Clear fix marked very low risk; only page views on this one address double.

cards.what: On slow phones, a piece listed since the last Publish shows its ivory outline while loading, instead of the homepage for about 5 seconds.
cards.shoppers: Shoppers on slow phones opening a newly listed piece no longer see the homepage ('Softly, slowly, worn.') before the product appears. Load times and everything else stay the same.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.why: Low-risk fix for a confusing flash on slow phones; Meta sees no change.

cards.what: Ads for a particular colour, metal, stone or month show that choice from the first moment the page appears, starting from the next Publish.
cards.shoppers: The Silver Triple Coil ad used to show the gold bangle, switching to silver about 2 to 3 seconds in; now silver shows from the start. Plain links load as before.
cards.meta: Nothing changes in what Meta is told.
cards.why: Fixes the wrong colour flashing first; Meta is told nothing new and a failure leaves the page as now.

cards.what: Adds the shop's shipping and return terms to the hidden product details of each jewellery page, so search results can show them.
cards.shoppers: Nothing changes on the page itself. Search results for jewellery may show free delivery and a 7-day return window; outfit pages are unchanged.
cards.meta: No events or values change. Meta's pixel reads this product data automatically, so it will see the added shipping and return details on every jewellery product page.
cards.ask: Should search results state free insured shipping in India, delivery in 3-5 working days and 7-day returns, given the FAQ's 3-7 days and the defects-only return policy?
cards.why: Search results would state these terms, and the site's own pages disagree on delivery time and returns.

cards.what: Links in Shopify's account emails and order pages, which now show 'Coming soon', would open the shop's Track Order page instead.
cards.shoppers: A shopper following a Shopify account link lands on Track Order, which explains that orders sit behind Shopify's sign-in. One more tap on Find My Order reaches that sign-in.
cards.meta: These visits now count two page views instead of one: the account address, then Track Order, with the ad's click id kept. No other events change.
cards.ask: Should Shopify account links open Track Order, one tap from sign-in (this option), go straight to Shopify's sign-in (Option 2), or keep showing Coming soon (neither)?
cards.why: Low risk, but it is one of two options and only one should be approved.

cards.what: Shopify customer-account links, such as order or password-reset links, now go straight to Shopify's own sign-in page.
cards.shoppers: Shoppers go straight to Shopify's sign-in, the page Track Order's Find My Order button opens; Back returns them to where they came from. If Shopify sends them back, they see Track Order.
cards.meta: These links stop sending Meta a page view, so Ads Manager may count fewer page views; any ad click id on them is not stored or passed on. Track Order, if shown instead, sends one.
cards.ask: Should Shopify account links go straight to Shopify's sign-in (this card) or show the shop's Track Order page (Option 1)?
cards.why: One of two options for these links; approve only this or 'Shopify customer-account links open Track Order', not both.

cards.what: A ring ad opens the product page on the ring size the ad names, when that size can be bought, instead of US 6.
cards.shoppers: A Tubogas Silver US 7 ad opens on US 7; two rings sold only by size lead with that size's photo. If stock changed since the last Publish, an ad can open a sold-out size with only Reserve now.
cards.meta: Add to cart and checkout start now name the ad's ring size instead of US 6, at the same prices; product views are unchanged. Where only Reserve now shows, neither is sent.
cards.ask: Should a ring ad open on the size it names (approve), or keep opening on US 6 and let the shopper pick (leave out)?
cards.why: Optional; builds on the catalogue ad change, and can open a sold-out size when stock is out of date.

corrections.problem: 'the matching real page' overstated it: about-us goes to the homepage, and cart, search and checkout go to the jewellery page, which are not matching pages. Changed to 'a real page on the shop'.

It left out a change shoppers can see and the risk text counts (25 kinds of address): /collections/dusk and /collections/frontpage now open the outfits page instead of the jewellery. Added it and stayed within 40 words.
'now count two page views' did not say that today there is one. Added 'instead of one' so the owner can see page views go up. Also made clear that the product view from an old collection link is new.

It said ads naming a metal or stone 'now' open on that choice. The full text shows main already opened the ad's metal and stone (Tubogas Silver, Gold, Baguette Ruby), and the meta text says only the birthstone month link changes. Rewrote it so the birthstone month is the one real change and rings stay on US 6.

'such a link' pointed back to nothing inside the field. It also left out the risk that tabs keeping no storage (some private modes) show Track Order instead of the sign-in. Named the link and added the private-mode case.
'only Reserve now' did not say what the shopper loses. The full text says those pages have no Add to cart or Buy Now. Added 'no Add to cart' so the owner sees the shopper cannot buy straight away.

'swaps to silver two to three seconds later' overstated the delay. The full text says the swap came about 2.1 to 2.9 seconds after the page started, not 2 to 3 seconds after the gold bangle appeared. Reworded to 'about 2 to 3 seconds in'.
Left out a Meta-related change the full text names: an ad click id carried on these links is no longer stored or passed to Shopify. Added it.

corrections.problem: The draft said only that white lettering becomes much easier to read. 'every product photo' overstated where the change happens. The full text places the badge only on product card photos, and the product page's own photos are not mentioned. It now says 'every product card photo'.

It named the change this card depends on with a made-up label, 'the footer and strip lettering fix', instead of its plain title, 'Dark lettering on the sage footer and the announcement strip'. Same made-up name for the change this card needs. It now uses that change's plain title, 'Dark lettering on the sage footer and the announcement strip'.
